ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Eva Perón Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient with four months of bleeding after intercourse and between periods and tiredness: history in Spanish, speculum examination, a visible cervical mass biopsied, HPV test and cytology, anemia tests, and her wishes about how results are given. Concerns: She has bled after intercourse and between periods for months and is exhausted, and she wants to know the cause; Whatever the results show, she wants to be told the truth herself, in Spanish, before anyone else is told; She wants to keep working and to understand how any treatment would affect her body and her chance of having children. [S]

list.item: Bleeding after intercourse and between periods, with heavier periods, for about four months, with tiredness and a dull pelvic ache. Never had cervical screening. Speculum examination shows a friable, exophytic mass about 4 cm across on the cervix that bleeds on contact. Punch biopsy, HPV test and cytology taken; urgent gynecologic oncology consultation booked: resolved, confirmed [S]
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs: resolved, confirmed [S]

Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, HPV 16 positive: an exophytic tumor about 4.5 cm across with clinical involvement of the left parametrium, not reaching the pelvic wall; pelvic MRI and PET-CT ordered for FIGO 2018 staging. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented cervical cancer: active, confirmed [S]

Acute cystitis during pelvic chemoradiation: two days of new burning, urgency and cloudy urine on top of mild radiation frequency, without fever or flank pain; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; neutrophil count and kidney function normal; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]
Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation, with hot flashes, night sweats, poor sleep and vaginal dryness two weeks after treatment; FSH 72 mIU/mL and estradiol 14 pg/mL: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient with four months of bleeding after intercourse and between periods and tiredness: history in Spanish, speculum examination, a visible cervical mass biopsied, HPV test and cytology, anemia tests, and her wishes about how results are given
Biopsy result given to her in person, and gynecologic oncology consultation the same day: diagnosis, staging plan, treatment options, and fertility and ovarian function counseling
Staging results (pelvic MRI and PET-CT), FIGO stage, and her treatment and fertility decisions before chemoradiation
Same-day sick visit for burning on passing urine during chemoradiation
Review two weeks after completing chemoradiation and brachytherapy: side effects, menopause symptoms, and survivorship care
Review three months after treatment: PET-CT response, examination, anemia, mood, and the follow-up plan
Periodic adult preventive visit after cancer treatment

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnosis of a visible cervical lesion: punch biopsy at this visit, an HPV test and cytology, a pregnancy test, a blood count and ferritin; a lesion that looks like cancer is biopsied directly rather than managed by the screening algorithm
Urgent gynecologic oncology consultation, on the day the biopsy result is given: diagnosis, staging, treatment by stage, and fertility and ovarian function counseling

Truthful disclosure as she asked: the biopsy result given to her in person, in Spanish, at a visit with time set aside, before anyone else is told; she chooses who is present and who is told; a professional medical interpreter for clinicians who do not speak Spanish, never a family member; information shared step by step, checking what she wants to know
Iron deficiency anemia: ferrous sulfate daily, a blood count at about one month, a ferritin at the end of the course, and acetaminophen rather than anti-inflammatory painkillers for pelvic pain
FIGO 2018 staging: pelvic MRI and FDG PET-CT, kidney function before cisplatin, an HIV test, and an examination of the vagina and parametria

Fertility and ovarian function counseling before treatment: chemoradiation ends the ability to carry a pregnancy and usually ends ovarian function; egg or embryo freezing (about two weeks), surgical moving of the ovaries out of the radiation field, and a gestational carrier were explained; her decision is recorded

Psychosocial support: the oncology social worker, the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at diagnosis, before treatment, at the end of treatment and in follow-up, spiritual care when she asks, and help planning work around treatment

Definitive chemoradiation for stage IIB disease: pelvic external beam radiation 45 Gy in 25 fractions with weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2, then image-guided high-dose-rate brachytherapy, all within eight weeks; weekly blood count, creatinine and magnesium; ondansetron for nausea and loperamide for diarrhea

Survivorship care: a vaginal dilator three times a week, estradiol with progesterone for radiation-induced menopause until the usual age of menopause, gynecologic oncology review every three months for two years, PET-CT about three months after treatment, and warning symptoms to report
Diagnosis and stage explained to her directly, in Spanish, with time for questions, before any treatment decision
Diagnosis given to her in person at the second visit and the stage at the third; she made the treatment and fertility decisions herself
Hemoglobin 10 g/dL or more before radiation begins
Chemoradiation and brachytherapy completed within eight weeks
Completed in eight weeks, with five cisplatin doses
No evidence of disease on PET-CT and examination three months after treatment
Complete metabolic response; examination without tumor
